text: D. C. Williams calls a particular property-instance, for example the redness of this single tomato, a ___, which he describes as an 'abstract particular'.
explanation: A trope is Williams's abstract particular: abstract because it is a property-aspect isolated from a full concretum, particular because it is numerically unique rather than shared. Bundles of compresent tropes make up concrete objects, and classes of exactly resembling tropes replace universals.
